newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to fine-tune debt with benchmark portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to fine-tune debt with benchmark portfolio.

text.p: The Belgian Treasury plans to introduce a benchmark debt portfolio, which will be used to improve management of the country's debt, Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Wednesday.
"Belgium will fine-tune the structure of its debt, following an 18-month study into how to minimise its cost," Maystadt told a parliamentary finance committee.
"I think we can say that the results up to now are relatively good, although it has shown us we have to change certain aspects," he said.

"One of the major conclusions of the analysis is that the actual structure of the public debt portfolio is reasonably close to the "benchmark' and it gives an adequate cost/risk ratio," the Treasury said in a statement presented to the committee.
With the benchmark portfolio, the Treasury will compare the actual structure of its debt against various theoretical models.

The portfolio, developed by the Treasury with the aid of advisers UBS and Morgan Stanley, assumes as its reference scenario that European economic and monetary union (EMU) will start in 1999 with Belgium as one of its members.

The other reference scenarios include EMU starting on time but after a period of market volatility, EMU being postponed to a later or imprecise date and EMU starting on time but with Belgium's entry anticipated in a second wave.
The parliament committee was due to question Maystadt all day. The Treasury has scheduled a news conference on Thursday to present details of the programme to the press.
